content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (IP), preferred level.**

The ownership architecture here is already strong — §14.2 (Customer owns / Vendor assigns Deliverables), §14.3 plus definition 1.9 (Vendor retains only pre-existing Vendor Technology), §14.1 (Customer owns Customer Data), §14.4 (no joint ownership without a signed instrument), and §13.2 (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to embedded Vendor Technology). Eight of the nine preferred elements are met verbatim.

The single material failure is the scope of Vendor's rights in Customer Data, which appears in three places:
1. §14.1 licensed processing "to provide, **secure, support, and improve**" the Services;
2. §15.1 permitted processing "**as permitted by this Agreement**" — an open-ended catch-all; and
3. §15.1's model-training prohibition was subject to a consent carve-out, which still contemplates a Vendor licence outside providing the Services.

Three surgical replacements narrow each expansion to processing solely to provide the Services, leaving every other word of the ownership and licence bargain untouched (validated `ok:true`, minimality passed).
